Subject: ACME - Model routing & policy integration: post-call next steps

Thanks again for your time today — great discussion. Quick recap + proposed next steps from Redwood: 

Recap (high level)
- ACME needs a model routing and policy layer to ensure low-latency responses for customer-facing flows while keeping inference costs bounded.
- Key constraints: SSO-enabled auth, VPC/private deployment for sensitive data, and regional routing (US-west primary, EU for EU traffic).
- Important features you called out: structured output & tool-calling for transactional flows, embeddings + reranker for search results, and failover policies for peak traffic.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (30-45m) to align on SDK/auth, routing policy knobs, and embedding/ indexer plan — please share availability next week.
2) I attached a draft model_routing_draft.yaml and an integration_diagram.png to start the config discussion.
3) Dev + Infra follow-up: we (Dev/Marcus) will propose a routing policy example with latency thresholds, fallback chains, and an A/B rollout suggestion for canarying.
4) Procurement/security: ACME to share procurement contact + security questionnaire (we can start a shared Drive).

Open questions for the deep-dive
- Do you expect single-tenant dedicated capacity or private VPC for this first phase?
- Typical tail latency SLA for the UI flows (p95 target)?
- How often do you plan to re-index embeddings (near-real-time vs nightly batch)?

Thanks — I’ll wait for a couple of times that work and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,

Adding some technical notes I’ll cover in the deep-dive and a short example policy snippet. Please review and flag anything missing.

Quick tech bullets
- SDK setup: we have language SDKs (Python/Node/Go). Quickstart: pip install redwood-sdk; set REDWOOD_API_URL and use OIDC (recommended) or API key for service accounts.
- Auth modes: API key (dev/testing), OIDC+aud claim (recommended for Prod + SSO). KMS for customer-managed keys in Private.
- Routing policy knobs: 
  * latency_threshold_ms: p95_target (e.g., 250)
  * cost_tier: low | medium | high — select cheaper quantized variants for cost_tier=low
  * region_preference: [us-west, us-east, eu-west]
  * fallback_chain: ordered list of compatible model variants to try on OOM/high-latency

Example (YAML stub):
- route_name: customer_ui
  latency_threshold_ms: 250
  preferred_model: gpt-instruct-medium
  cost_tier: medium
  region_preference: [us-west]
  fallback_chain: [gpt-instruct-small-quant, gpt-instruct-small]
  canary: true
  canary_traffic_pct: 10

Embeddings / reranker notes
- Indexing: realtime for priority docs (webhook triggers) + nightly batch for archive.
- Reranker: runtime rerank on top-50 with a small cross-encoder model for quality-sensitive flows. We recommend caching reranker scores for 24h to reduce cost.
- Batching: continuous batching for token generation; for embeddings we batch by 128 vectors to maximize throughput.

Attachments: model_routing_draft.yaml (policy examples, more details)

I’ll bring a concrete implementation example to the call (code snippets + config).
